name: granularity-required-absent-one-per-member
note: Section 10 row 1. Two of three required members are absent: one violation each, in the listed order of required, focusPath the object, constraintPath the member, constraintId from requiredIds when declared (null when not). A runtime that reports the shape once, or in another order, fails.

name: granularity-field-primitive-failure-one-per-member
note: Section 10 row 2. Two present members fail their own keyword check (a minimum, an enum): one violation each, focusPath the object, constraintPath the member, in code-point order of the field names. Nothing is reported for the members that pass.

name: granularity-nested-shape-is-its-own-target
note: Section 10 row 3. A member checked against a named shape runs that shape as its own target: the violation's focusPath is the member's path and its constraintPath is the nested member that failed. The parent gets no violation of its own for the member (no constraintPath [customer]).

name: granularity-nested-check-failure-has-no-constraint-path
note: Section 10 rows 3 and 4 together. The nested shape's own check fails: one violation, focusPath the nested node, shape the nested shape, constraintId from its check, and constraintPath absent (not null).

name: granularity-check-failure-is-one-violation
note: Section 10 row 4. A shape's own check fails: exactly one violation at the shape's focus node, with the check's id, the shape's message, and no constraintPath.

name: granularity-or-failure-is-one-violation-for-the-whole-shape
note: Section 10 row 5 and section 4. No alternative of an or passes: exactly one violation, carrying the enclosing shape's message, never one per alternative.

name: granularity-and-failure-is-one-violation-for-the-whole-shape
note: Section 10 row 5. Two alternatives of an and would fail; evaluation stops at the first, and the shape yields one violation.

name: granularity-xone-failure-is-one-violation-for-the-whole-shape

Size.message: must exceed exactly one of 100 and 1000

violations.message: must exceed exactly one of 100 and 1000

note: Section 10 row 5. Exactly one is required and two alternatives match: one violation for the shape.

name: granularity-not-failure-is-one-violation
note: Section 10 row 5. A not whose inner shape matches: one violation for the shape.

name: granularity-unique-flags-each-repeat-not-the-first
note: Section 10 row 6 and section 7. In target-visiting order the first occurrence of each key is never flagged; every later element sharing a key is, at its own path. Five lines, keys a b a a b: violations at indices 2, 3 and 4.

name: severity-warning-does-not-flip-conforms
note: Section 10: conforms reflects violation-severity findings only. The same repeats at severity warning are all reported and conforms stays true.

name: severity-info-does-not-flip-conforms-and-a-violation-does
note: Section 10. An info finding and a violation in one combined report: both are listed, in the order the entries ran, and conforms is false because of the violation alone.

name: minimal-or-stops-at-first-pass
note: Section 4. or stops at the first passing alternative. 500 passes IsBig, so Boom (which raises TYPE_ERROR whenever it is evaluated) is never reached and the run conforms. A runtime that evaluates every alternative raises instead.

name: minimal-or-continues-while-alternatives-fail
note: Control for the previous fixture: IsHuge fails for 500, so or must go on to Boom, which raises. Shows Boom really is reachable and the previous fixture passes for the stated reason.

name: minimal-and-stops-at-first-failure
note: Section 4. and stops at the first failing alternative. 5 fails IsHuge, so Boom is never evaluated: one violation, no error.

name: minimal-and-continues-while-alternatives-pass
note: Control: 500 passes IsBig, so and goes on to Boom, which raises.

name: minimal-xone-stops-at-second-match
note: Section 4. xone stops as soon as a second match is found. 5000 matches IsBig and IsHuge, so Boom is never evaluated: one violation for the shape.

name: minimal-xone-continues-after-one-match
note: Control: after a single match xone cannot yet decide, so it must evaluate the next alternative. 500 matches IsBig only; Boom is then evaluated and raises.

name: extends-parent-alternatives-are-evaluated-first
note: Section 4, extends merge rule: the parent's or-list comes before the child's. The parent's IsBig passes for 500, so the child's Boom is never reached.

name: extends-child-alternatives-follow-the-parent-s
note: Control: the parent's IsHuge fails for 500, so the pooled or goes on to the child's Boom, which raises. Shows the pool really is parent-then-child.

name: extends-xone-pools-and-can-turn-a-pass-into-a-failure
note: Section 4. Exactly one is evaluated over the merged pool, not the child's list alone: 5000 matches the child's IsHuge (so exactly one of the child's own list) and the parent's IsBig, so the pool matches two and fails.

name: extends-xone-pool-passes-when-exactly-one-matches
note: Control: 500 matches only the parent's IsBig, so the pooled xone holds.

name: gate-checks-required-before-fields
note: Section 10. Gate mode goes required, then fields, then check, and stops at the first failure. a is absent, so the run fails with SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR before the field b (a shape that raises TYPE_ERROR if evaluated) is looked at.

name: gate-checks-fields-before-check
note: Section 10. Required passes, field b fails its kind, and the check (which raises TYPE_ERROR on a string) is never evaluated: SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR, not EXECUTION_ERROR.

name: gate-visits-fields-in-code-point-order
note: Section 10. Fields are visited in code-point order, so B (0x42) comes before a (0x61) although a is declared first and sorts first case-insensitively. B holds a shape that raises, a fails its kind: reaching B first means EXECUTION_ERROR, reaching a first would mean SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR.

name: gate-stops-before-the-program-runs
note: Section 7. A gate failure aborts the pipeline and the program does not run. The program here would fail an assert if it ran, which would be a different error category.

name: report-lists-required-in-declared-order
note: Section 10. Absent required members are reported in the order required lists them (z before a), not sorted.

name: report-lists-failing-fields-in-code-point-order
note: Section 10. Failing fields are reported in code-point order of their names (B, a, z) regardless of the order they are declared in.

name: report-orders-required-then-fields-then-check
note: Section 10. When a required member is absent, a field fails and the check fails in one object, a report lists them in the gate's order: required, fields, check. The check carries no constraintPath.

name: unique-gate-first-repeat-aborts-and-program-does-not-run
note: Section 7. In gate mode the first element that repeats an already seen key aborts with SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR/SHAX_SHAPE_MISMATCH and the program does not run (it would fail an assert).

name: unique-gate-without-a-repeat-lets-the-program-run
note: Control: no repeat, so the gate passes and the program runs.

name: unique-checks-the-element-itself-for-scalars
note: Section 7. For non-object elements the element itself is the key. 1 2 1 2 1: the repeats are at indices 2, 3 and 4; the first 1 and the first 2 are never flagged.

name: unique-over-an-object-visits-in-sorted-key-order
note: Sections 7 and 7 (target order). Elements of an object are visited in code-point order of their keys, so the first occurrence of the value is the one under key a, and the later one under key b is the repeat, though b is written first.

name: unique-with-no-repeats-conforms
note: Section 7. Distinct keys give an empty violation list and conforms true.

name: unique-and-shape-in-one-entry-is-a-shape-error
note: Sections 7 and 9. An entry declaring both shape and unique is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR, before anything runs.

name: qualified-elements-that-do-not-match-are-not-violations
note: Section 4. qualified counts matching elements; an element that fails the qualified shape is not itself a finding. Three elements, one matches, min 1: conforms with an empty violation list.

name: qualified-minimum-is-inclusive
note: Section 4. Exactly min matching elements satisfies qualified (gate mode, so a miss would be an error).

name: qualified-maximum-is-inclusive
note: Section 4. Exactly max matching elements satisfies qualified.

name: qualified-below-minimum-fails
note: Section 4. One matching element where min is 2: the gate aborts.

name: qualified-above-maximum-fails
note: Section 4. Four matching elements where max is 3: the gate aborts.

name: qualified-is-not-a-step-cost-exemption
note: Section 4. Each element checked against qualified's shape is charged the ordinary shape-evaluation cost, as if checked individually. Forty elements each run the shape's check (at least one step each), so a limit of 15 steps cannot hold; a runtime that counts qualified elements for free would finish inside it.

name: qualified-cost-follows-the-number-of-elements
note: Control for the previous fixture, same limit: an empty array has no elements to charge for, so the run stays inside 15 steps. Shows the charge is per element and the limit is not simply too low.

name: qualified-cost-control-with-a-generous-limit
note: Control: the forty-element package of the cost fixture finishes with the default limit, so the failure above is the step charge and nothing else.

name: reference-report-gives-each-dangling-element-its-own-violation

violations.message: referenced value is not present in the named index
referenced value is not present in the named index

note: Section 5. In report mode every dangling element is its own structural violation at that element's path, never one aggregate: two of four tag ids are absent from the index, so two violations, at indices 1 and 3, in array order. code SHAX_DANGLING_REFERENCE, the fixed message and severity, and shape the named shape being checked (Order), not the inline reference item.

name: reference-all-present-conforms
note: Control: every tag id is in the index.

name: reference-gate-first-dangling-aborts-with-dangling-reference
note: Section 5. In gate mode the first dangling element in array order raises SHAX_DANGLING_REFERENCE and aborts, an EXECUTION_ERROR code (section 9), not a SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR.

name: reference-non-scalar-value-is-type-error
note: Section 5. A reference value that is an object or array is TYPE_ERROR, not a dangling finding, even in report mode.

name: reference-array-value-is-type-error
note: Section 5. An array is as non-scalar as an object: TYPE_ERROR.

name: reference-resolves-against-the-to-side-of-a-relation

violations.message: referenced value is not present in the named index

note: Sections 4a and 5. {kind: reference, relation: name} checks against the relation's to side: the link to tag zz is dangling, the link to a is not.

name: reference-inline-of-by-shorthand

violations.message: referenced value is not present in the named index

note: Section 4a. The inline shorthand {kind: reference, of: path, by: [field]} behaves as an anonymous index over that path keyed by that field.

name: index-repeated-key-without-multi-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 3. Without multi, a repeated key is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR at build time: an index is a function unless declared otherwise.

name: index-repeated-key-with-multi-is-allowed
note: Section 3. With multi: true the same input is a valid index; the reference check passes.

name: index-key-that-is-not-scalar-is-type-error
note: Section 3. A key expression resolving to an object or array for any source element is TYPE_ERROR.

name: index-key-that-does-not-resolve-is-missing-path
note: Section 3. A key expression that fails to resolve for any element is MISSING_PATH; no element is silently skipped.

name: relation-repeated-to-key-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 4a. The to side is the unique side: a repeated to.key value is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR, as for any non-multi index.

name: relation-one-to-one-rejects-a-repeated-from-field
note: Section 4a. one-to-one also requires uniqueness on from.field; two links to tag a violate it: SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR.

name: relation-one-to-one-does-not-require-every-target-to-be-referenced
note: Section 4a. one-to-one does not require that every to element be referenced: tag b has no link and the run conforms.

name: relation-redundant-with-the-inline-shorthand-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 4c. An inline {of, by} shorthand whose normalised (path, key) equals the to side of a relation is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR at load; the author should write {relation} instead.

name: two-relations-with-the-same-to-side-are-a-shape-error
note: Section 4c. Two relations whose to sides normalise to the same (path, key) are SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR at load.

name: required-ids-key-not-in-required-is-a-shape-error
note: Sections 4 and 9. A requiredIds key naming a member that is not in required is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR.

name: enum-on-an-object-kind-is-a-shape-error
note: Sections 4 and 9. enum is legal only on string, number, boolean and null kinds.

name: enum-on-a-number-matches-exact-values
note: Section 4. enum on a number kind: a listed value passes, any other fails, under the same exact-match rule as strings.

name: index-build-costs-at-least-one-step-per-source-element
note: Section 3. An index build costs one step per source element visited. Sixty elements cannot be built within 59 steps, whatever else the run costs.

name: index-build-costs-no-more-than-about-one-step-per-element
note: Upper-bound control for the previous fixture, on the same package: with 80 steps (60 for the build plus a margin for the rest of the run) it finishes. A runtime charging two steps per element would need 120. The margin of 20 assumes a single reference lookup and the trivial program cost under 20 steps; the core fixes only the build charge.

name: index-build-is-reused-when-no-mutation-touched-its-source
note: Section 3. Reuse is mandatory: three validate entries use the same index and nothing mutates its source, so it is built once (60 steps), not three times (180). With 100 steps the run finishes only if the build is reused.

name: index-build-is-repeated-when-its-source-was-written
note: Section 3. A mutation of the source itself forces a rebuild: the program writes the indexed array between two gate checks, so the index is built twice (120 steps) and a limit of 100 is exceeded. Control for the reuse fixture: shows the same limit fails when the rule requires a rebuild.

name: index-sees-data-written-by-the-program
note: Section 3. Indices are rebuilt from their declared source before every use so a program that mutates state is always validated against current data. The first check passes, the program then removes the tag from state, and the second check fails with SHAX_DANGLING_REFERENCE.

name: indexed-target-visits-a-non-multi-index-in-ascending-key-order
note: Section 7. $indexed makes every source element its own focus node, never the key or value; for a non-multi index the elements are visited in ascending key order, not array order. Keys c, a, b sit at indices 0, 1, 2; the (always failing) shape's violations come out at indices 1, 2, 0.

name: indexed-target-visits-a-multi-index-grouped-by-key-then-array-order
note: Section 7. For a multi index the elements are grouped by key in ascending key order, then in array-index order within a key. Keys o2 o1 o2 o1 at indices 0..3 give the order 1, 3 (o1) then 0, 2 (o2). Every element is visited exactly once.

name: inverse-yields-the-paths-of-the-matching-elements-in-array-order
note: Section 6. $inverse over a multi index yields every path the index maps the key to, in the index's own iteration order (array order within a key).

name: inverse-of-an-absent-key-is-an-empty-list
note: Section 6. A key the multi index does not hold yields an empty path list, not an error.

name: closure-star-is-the-base-then-each-extension-breadth-first
note: Section 6. $path* visits the base and then every reachable extension, stopping (not erroring) the first time a hop does not resolve. Base list, then next, then next.next.

name: closure-plus-is-the-star-sequence-without-the-base
note: Section 6. $path+ is the same sequence minus the base.

name: closure-step-may-cross-several-fields-as-one-hop
note: Section 6. A multi-segment innerStep is a single hop. With step [next, next] the nodes are base, then two fields down; the maxDepth of 1 counts that as one hop and is not exceeded.

name: closure-without-max-depth-is-a-program-error
note: Section 6. maxDepth is mandatory on both closure forms; its absence is a static PROGRAM_ERROR, before anything runs.

name: closure-within-its-horizon-is-silent
note: Section 6. A chain that ends before maxDepth is reached produces no finding: stopping at an unresolvable hop is not an error.

name: closure-beyond-its-horizon-is-a-structural-violation-in-report-mode
note: Section 6. Exceeding maxDepth while the chain still resolves further is SHAX_PATH_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, a violation and not a silent stop: structural, with the fixed message and severity. Chain of 6 hops, maxDepth 3.

name: closure-beyond-its-horizon-raises-in-gate-mode
note: Sections 6 and 9. The same overrun in gate mode raises EXECUTION_ERROR/SHAX_PATH_DEPTH_EXCEEDED (distinct from SHAX_SHAPE_DEPTH_EXCEEDED).

name: altpath-takes-the-first-alternative-that-resolves
note: Section 6. $altPath yields the first alternative that resolves, even when a later one also does.

name: altpath-falls-through-to-a-later-alternative
note: Section 6. When the first alternative does not resolve the next is used.

name: altpath-with-no-resolving-alternative-is-missing-path
note: Section 6. MISSING_PATH only if none of the alternatives resolves.

name: recursion-without-max-shape-depth-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 2. maxShapeDepth is mandatory whenever a shape can recurse; its absence is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR, not a silent default.

name: recursion-within-max-shape-depth-conforms
note: Section 2. With a declared bound that is not reached, a recursive shape validates normally.

name: recursion-past-max-shape-depth-is-a-structural-violation
note: Sections 2 and 10. Recursion past maxShapeDepth is SHAX_SHAPE_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, reportable: structural, with the fixed message and severity. A chain ten shapes deep against a bound of 2 (what exactly counts as one level is not fixed by the core, so the margin is wide).

name: recursion-past-max-shape-depth-raises-in-gate-mode
note: Sections 2 and 9. In gate mode the overrun raises EXECUTION_ERROR/SHAX_SHAPE_DEPTH_EXCEEDED.

name: extends-cycle-is-a-shape-error
note: Sections 4 and 9. An extends cycle is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR.

name: extends-field-name-collision-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 4, merge rule. A name collision in fields is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR unless the child marks the field override.

name: extends-field-override-replaces-the-parent-definition
note: Section 4, merge rule. With override: true on the child's field the child's definition replaces the parent's: a is now a string, so the number 1 fails it.

name: extends-required-is-the-union-of-parent-and-child
note: Section 4, merge rule. required accumulates: the parent requires a, the child requires b, and both are reported when absent, parent's first.

name: extends-check-of-parent-and-child-are-both-applied
note: Section 4, merge rule. check: the parent's and the child's are ANDed. The value passes the parent's (positive) and fails the child's (below 10): exactly the child's check is reported.

name: closure-ending-exactly-at-its-horizon-is-silent
note: Section 6. A chain of exactly maxDepth hops (3 of 3) is within the horizon: no SHAX_PATH_DEPTH_EXCEEDED. Boundary pair with the next fixture.

name: closure-one-hop_past-its-horizon-is-a-structural-violation
note: Section 6. One hop more (4 resolving hops, maxDepth 3) is the overrun. The boundary is at maxDepth, not one past it.

name: closure-through-a-null-link-still-resolves-and-can-overrun
note: Section 6. A chain stops at the first hop that does not resolve. A member that is present and holds null resolves, so a null-terminated list is one hop longer than it looks: head.next.next.next is null, the third hop resolves, and with maxDepth 2 that is the overrun. (Found while rewriting an attic fixture whose list ended in a null link.)

name: closed-is-the-default-posture
note: Section 4. Closed objects are the default: a member no field declares is rejected (gate mode: SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR).

name: closed-false-allows-undeclared-members
note: Section 4. closed: false allows members the fields do not declare.

name: ignored-properties-are-exempt-from-closed
note: Section 4. A name in ignoredProperties is allowed on a closed object; any other undeclared member is still rejected. Here only $meta is undeclared, so the run conforms.

name: ignored-properties-do-not-exempt-other-members
note: Control: with $meta ignored, a second undeclared member (extra) still fails a closed object.

name: each-primitive-keyword-fails-as-its-own-member-violation
note: Sections 4 and 10, row 2. Keywords inherited from Jaxson's narrow vocabulary (minLen, maxLen, min, max, minItems, maxItems) each fail as a primitive check on their member: one violation per member, constraintPath the member, in code-point order of the member names (a b m n s t).

name: field-shape-id-becomes-the-constraint-id
note: Section 10. constraintId is settable via an id member on a field shape: the field's primitive failure carries it; a failing field with no id carries null.

name: wrong-kind-on-a-member-is-a-primitive-failure
note: Section 10, row 2. A member of the wrong kind (a string where a number is declared) fails as one primitive violation on that member.

name: missing-shaxon-key-is-a-version-error
note: Section 2. shaxon is mandatory; its absence is VERSION_ERROR before anything else runs.

name: an-unsupported-version-is-a-version-error
note: Section 2. A runtime that does not implement a declared version rejects it with VERSION_ERROR. 9.9 is not a version any runtime implements.

name: a-jaxson-key-instead-of-shaxon-is-a-version-error
note: Sections 2 and 9. A package that declares only the jaxson key is not a Shaxon package: VERSION_ERROR. (The compatibility shim of section 9 is a separate component, not the Shaxon runtime.)

name: a-version-that-is-not-a-string-is-a-version-error
note: Section 2. The version is a string; the number 3.1 is not the string "3.1".

name: an-unknown-limits-member-is-a-version-error
note: Section 1 (Jaxson carries over). An unknown member of limits is rejected before anything runs.

name: static-shape-error-is-reported-before-an-input-gate-failure
note: Section 9, pipeline order. Shapes are checked statically before the input is validated: a malformed shape (enum on an object) wins over an input that would also fail the gate.

name: program-validation-precedes-the-input-gate
note: Section 9, pipeline order. The program is validated before the input is checked: an unknown instruction is PROGRAM_ERROR even though the input would fail its gate.

name: output-gate-is-not-reached-when-the-program-fails
note: Section 9, pipeline order. Output gate-shapes run after execution and an earlier failure means later stages do not run: the program fails its assert, so the output shape (which raises TYPE_ERROR if evaluated) is never reached.

name: output-gate-runs-after-the-program-has-written-the-output
note: Control for the previous fixture, and section 9 pipeline order: with a program that succeeds the output shape is reached and evaluated (Boom raises TYPE_ERROR on the number the program wrote).

name: output-gate-failure-is-a-validation-error
note: Sections 7 and 9. An output-rooted gate that fails after execution is SHAX_VALIDATION_ERROR/SHAX_SHAPE_MISMATCH, the generalisation of OUTPUT_ERROR.

name: check-sees-the-state-the-program-just-wrote
note: Section 8. check asserts a shape against current state: after the program writes -1 to state.n the gate fails.

name: check-passes-on-conforming-state-and-the-program-continues
note: Control: with 1 written to state.n the gate passes and the program goes on to write its output.

name: check-gate-failure-stops-the-program
note: Sections 7 and 8. A gate-mode check that fails aborts: the assert after it never runs (it would raise a different error).

name: check-in-report-mode-without-into-never-aborts-and-leaves-state-alone
note: Section 8. A report-mode check without into collects its findings into the combined report and the program continues; with no into, nothing is delivered into a root, so state is exactly as the program made it (output is read back from state and holds only n).

name: report-entries-and-checks-without-into-combine-in-execution-order
note: Section 7, last bullet. A validate entry that runs before the program and a check inside it, both without into, contribute to one combined report in the order they executed: the validate entry's finding first, the check's second.

name: validate-into-writes-the-report-and-returns-none-alongside-output
note: Section 7. A report-mode validate entry with into writes the report object to that path, in the full section 10 form (conforms and violations, each violation with focusPath, kind, shape, constraintId, severity, message, code; constraintPath absent for a shape check), and nothing is returned alongside output.

name: only-entries-without-into-reach-the-returned-report
note: Section 7. Of two report-mode entries, the one with into delivers to its path and the one without is returned alongside output: the returned report holds only the second entry's finding.

name: attic-index-build-is-charged-per-element-inside-a-loop
note: 8-element index, rebuilt before each of 2 check calls. Program-instruction cost alone is ~5 steps, well under the declared limit of 10 — this fixture only fails to stay under budget if index (re)builds are charged one step per source element, per v0.1.1 section 3. An interpreter that treats index builds as free will produce 'output' instead of this error, which is exactly the gap this fixture exists to catch. [Mined from attic/ fixture 'check-in-loop-must-charge-index-rebuild-steps' (declared 1.1); rewritten for 3.1: version string only. The original expected a rebuild before each of the two checks; under the mandatory reuse rule of section 3 the index is built once, 8 steps, which together with the program's own cost still exceeds the limit of 10, so the expected result is unchanged and now rests on the build charge alone.]

name: attic-closure-target-reports-the-failing-node-mid-chain
note: Exercises $path* as a section-7 target form (v0.1.1 section 6/7): the closure {head, head.next, head.next.next} is visited (0..maxDepth=2 hops along the relative step ['next']), each node checked against PositiveNode, and only the depth-2 node (value -1) violates. Also exercises the explicit 'from' base a closure needs when used as a target, versus an ambient focus/item when embedded elsewhere. [Mined from attic/ fixture 'path-plus-closure-target-reports-violation-mid-chain' (declared 1.1); rewritten for 3.1: from is a plain path array (section 6), the terminating null link is removed so that the chain ends at the horizon rather than resolving past it (a null value still resolves, which section 6 would report as SHAX_PATH_DEPTH_EXCEEDED), and the check has no into: its report is the combined report returned alongside output; PositiveNode is declared closed: false, because the original relied on nodes with an undeclared next member being allowed, which closed-by-default (section 4) no longer does.]

name: attic-relation-gives-forward-reference-and-inverse-paths
note: One 'relations' entry stands in for the hand-written pair from v0.0.1 (a customersById index + reference field, plus a separate ordersByCustomer multi index + $inverse call). Confirms the forward direction (every order's customerId resolves against customers.id via 'relation', not a named index) and the reverse direction ($inverse by 'relation' returns exactly the orders for customer 1) round-trip correctly through the desugaring in v0.1.1's new relations section. [Mined from attic/ fixture 'relations-block-desugars-to-forward-reference-and-inverse-lookup' (declared 1.1); rewritten for 3.1: $inverse yields paths (section 6), not the elements the original expected, so the expected output is the two order paths in array order; the program first sets output to an empty object, because a member cannot be set on a null output.]

name: attic-extends-pools-xone-alternatives

StrictPositive.message: must be exactly one of even or positive, pooled with what extends contributes

violations.message: must be exactly one of even or positive, pooled with what extends contributes

note: n=4 matches both IsEven and IsPositive. Against StrictPositive's own xone list alone (just IsPositive) this would trivially pass — nothing else in a one-element list to conflict with. Once extends pools HasXone's alternative in (section 4), the merged xone list is [IsEven, IsPositive], both match, and 'exactly one' fails. An interpreter that merges only fields/closed per the old v0.0.1 wording and treats xone as child-only would report conforms:true here instead — the gap this fixture exists to catch. name: extends-closed-and-needs-both-parent-and-child-closed
note: Section 4, merge rule. closed accumulates by AND: the parent is closed (the default) and the child declares closed: false, so the merged shape is still closed and rejects the undeclared member.

name: extends-closed-override-lets-the-child-win
note: Section 4, merge rule. closedOverride: true makes the child's own closed value win outright: with the same shapes as the previous fixture the undeclared member is now allowed.

name: extends-explicit-closed-child-closes-an-open-parent
note: Section 4, merge rule. closed accumulates as the most restrictive of parent and child: an open parent (closed: false) extended by a child that states closed: true gives a closed shape, so the undeclared member is rejected.

name: extends-and-pools-without-override
note: Section 4, merge rule. and concatenates the parent's list and the child's: 500 passes the child's IsBig but fails the parent's IsHuge, so the pooled and fails.

name: extends-and-override-replaces-the-parent-list
note: Section 4, merge rule. andOverride: true on the child replaces the parent's list: only IsBig applies, and 500 passes.

name: extends-or-override-replaces-the-parent-list
note: Section 4, merge rule. orOverride: true replaces instead of pooling. Pooled, 500 would pass the parent's IsBig; replaced, only the child's IsHuge applies and 500 fails it.

name: extends-xone-override-replaces-the-parent-list
note: Section 4, merge rule. xoneOverride: true replaces instead of pooling. Pooled, 5000 matches two (the previous groups showed that); replaced, exactly one (the child's IsHuge) matches and the run conforms.

name: extends-not-applies-both-parent-and-child
note: Section 4, merge rule. not: both targets apply, so the focus must satisfy neither. 500 is big, which the parent's not forbids.

name: extends-not-override-replaces-the-parent-s
note: Section 4, merge rule. notOverride: true replaces the parent's not: only the child's not IsHuge applies, and 500 is not huge, so it conforms.

name: extends-check-override-replaces-the-parent-check
note: Section 4, merge rule. checkOverride on the child replaces the parent's check instead of ANDing: -5 fails the parent's positivity check but the parent's check no longer applies, and passes the child's negativity check.

name: extends-check-without-override-keeps-both
note: Control: the same shapes with the child's check written as an ordinary check are ANDed, so -5 fails the parent's positivity check.

name: check-and-check-override-on-one-shape-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 4, merge rule. checkOverride stands in for the shape's own check; declaring both on one shape is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR.

name: extends-required-ids-collision-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 4, merge rule. requiredIds is a union by key and a key in both parent and child is SHAX_SHAPE_ERROR unless the child's entry is overridden.

name: extends-required-ids-override-uses-the-object-form
note: Section 4, merge rule. A child entry written {value, override: true} replaces the parent's id for that key: the absence of a is reported under CHILD_ID.

name: extends-required-ids-union-keeps-the-parent-id
note: Section 4, merge rule. With no collision the parent's id is kept: the child adds an id for a different member, and the parent's member still reports under PARENT_ID.

name: override-outside-a-field-or-required-id-is-a-shape-error
note: Section 4, merge rule. override is legal only inside a field definition or a requiredIds entry; anywhere else it is rejected as an unknown key. Here it sits on the shape itself.

name: aggregate-counts-sums-and-finds-the-extremes
note: Section 8a. The four measures over one array: count, sum, min and max of the elements, written to the members the measures name.

name: aggregate-where-leaves-out-the-elements-it-rejects
note: Section 8a. Only elements for which where is true contribute: the 12 and the -2 are excluded by x > 2 and x < 10, so only 3 and 8 are counted, summed and compared.

name: aggregate-over-an-empty-array-is-zero-zero-null-null
note: Section 8a. With no contributing element count and sum are 0, and min and max are null (not an error, and not 0).

name: aggregate-where-false-for-every-element-is-the-empty-result
note: Section 8a. A where that rejects everything gives the same result as an empty array.

name: aggregate-sum-is-exact-decimal
note: Section 8a. sum is the exact sum: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3, as in the compute sublanguage.

name: aggregate-extremes-of-decimals-and-negatives
note: Section 8a. min and max compare numbers, not text: -10 is below -9.5, and 0.5 is above -1.

name: aggregate-replaces-whatever-was-at-into
note: Section 8a. The result is written as a set: members the measures do not name, and a previous n, are gone.

name: aggregate-measure-names-may-be-anything-a-member-can-be
note: Section 8a. Measure names are members of the result object and need not look like identifiers.

name: aggregate-inside-a-loop-and-a-branch
note: Section 8a. aggregate is usable wherever an instruction is: here inside an if inside a for, once per row.

name: aggregate-costs-exactly-what-its-expansion-costs
note: Section 8a. An aggregate is sugar and has no cost of its own. This fixture and the next run the same fold, one as aggregate and one written out by hand, and both are pinned to the same step total (18 under the unit table).

name: aggregate-hand-written-fold-has-the-same-cost
note: Section 8a. The hand-written fold the previous fixture stands for: same output, same 18 steps.

name: aggregate-is-bounded-by-the-step-limit-like-any-loop
note: Section 8a. The expansion is an ordinary loop and is charged as one: eight elements and a limit of 10 steps exhaust the budget.

name: aggregate-sum-of-a-non-number-is-a-type-error
note: Section 8a. sum, min and max operands must be numbers; a string is the TYPE_ERROR the compute operators raise.

name: aggregate-min-of-a-non-number-is-a-type-error
note: Section 8a. The same for min, even when the non-number is the only element: no later comparison would have caught it, so the operand itself must be checked.

name: aggregate-without-measures-is-a-program-error
note: Section 8a. measures is required.

name: aggregate-with-empty-measures-is-a-program-error
note: Section 8a. measures must not be empty.

name: aggregate-with-an-unknown-measure-is-a-program-error
note: Section 8a. There is no avg: a measure is one of count, sum, min, max.

name: aggregate-measure-with-two-kinds-is-a-program-error
note: Section 8a. A measure holds exactly one of the four kinds.

name: aggregate-count-takes-only-true
note: Section 8a. count is written {"count": true}; anything else is rejected.

name: aggregate-with-an-unknown-member-is-a-program-error
note: Section 8a. An aggregate has in, as, into, where and measures and nothing else.

name: aggregate-into-input-is-a-program-error
note: Section 8a. into is written like a set: input is read-only, so it is refused before anything runs.

name: aggregate-binding-may-not-shadow-an-outer-one
note: Section 8a. as is an ordinary for binding and follows the shadowing rule: inside a for over x it cannot be x again.
